title: introduce-selective-prebuild-cache-and-node-virtualization-to-accelerate-ci-lints
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: CI latency has regressed for PRs touching JS/TS packages due to full node_modules installs and repeated heavy prebuild steps. This PR introduces a selective prebuild artifact cache plus a light node_modules virtualization layer to avoid full installs for unchanged dependency graphs. Goals: 1) reduce cold CI job time for lint and unit jobs by caching prebuild artifacts keyed to repo subgraph hash, 2) avoid mismatched caches by including package lock signature and toolchain stamp, 3) provide a safe rollback path and opt-out per job. Design summary: A new cache indexer (ci/cache/indexer.ts) computes a deterministic subgraph hash by scanning package.json/package-lock.json and the subset of files referenced by each package. The cache producer stores prebuilt artifacts (dist, native addons build outputs, compiled protojs) in the shared CI object store under keys: prebuild/{subgraph-hash}/{toolchain-stamp}. A lightweight node virtualization shim (ci/virtual-nm/README.md and tools/virtual-nm-runner.ts) mounts an ephemeral symlinked layout that reuses cached prebuilds without materializing the full node_modules. We also introduce cache pruning: a nightly job prunes entries older than 30 days and keeps at most 200 recent hashes per repo using LRU heuristics. Backwards compatibility: default workflows opt into the cache via a new workflow input fastpath-cache: true. Existing workflows remain unchanged until we flip the fastpath in CI config. Security: artifacts are signed with the CI signing key; the verifier rejects unsigned artifacts during restore. Rollout plan: enable for lint/unit lanes first with a controlled percentage rollout across CI pools then expand to integration lanes pending metrics. Checklist: - [x] cache indexer prototype and unit tests - [x] producer/consumer steps for GitHub Actions - [x] virtualization shim with fallbacks to npm/yarn install - [x] cache pruning job and retention configuration - [x] docs and migration guide in ci/cache/README.md - [x] Linear tickets linked for rollout and monitoring Implementation notes: commits include the indexer, the producer action wrapper, the consumer step, virtualization shim, CI workflow changes for main lint and unit jobs, and docs. Local dev: tools/virtual-nm-runner.ts has a --dry-run that simulates layout changes; indexer has --print-hash for reproducibility checks. Testing: unit tests for indexer and virtual-nm run under node 18 and 20 in CI matrix; integrated smoke runs used internal testbed with a synthetic monorepo described in ci/cache/testcases/; e2e rollout staged to small subset of runners. Risks and mitigations: cache key collision avoided by including package-lock and Node toolchain stamp, cache poisoning mitigated via artifact signature and server-side ACLs. If the virtualization shim fails, job falls back to normal install and emits a diagnostic artifact to help debugging. Observability: added metric ci.prebuild_cache.hit_ratio and ci.prebuild_cache.restore_latency, and a dashboard tile with rollout percent. Rollback: revert the workflow input or the feature gate in the console; nightly prune continues to run but will not affect non-adopters. Related work: builds on ENG-4230 (previous lightweight cache experiment) and differs by focusing on per-subgraph keys and virtualization instead of workspace-level caches. See linked tickets for rollout schedule. Merge outcome: merged to main via squash after CI stabilized and two approvals.

review_comments: Ethan Park: Can we avoid adding the node toolchain stamp for every small change? Suggest we only include it when toolchain changes are detected. Author: the indexer inspects .nvmrc and lockfile's engine fields and will only include the stamp when mismatch is present.

María Gómez: Please add an integration test that simulates a corrupted artifact restore. Author: added a corrupted-restore testcase under ci/cache/testcases and a verifier unit test that asserts failure and fallback behavior.

Luca Rossi: Concern about increased storage costs. Can we set tighter retention? Author: introduced repo-level retention and cap of 200 recent hashes with nightly pruning; added metrics to monitor storage usage.
Ethan Park: CI shows a flaky integration run on first upload attempt. Author: retried uploads with exponential backoff and added upload verification; subsequent CI run passed.
María Gómez: Approve with minor docs nit. Author: fixed docs nit and added an upgrade step for internal tooling.
ci_checks: integration-smoke: pass after retry (first attempt failed on upload)
release_notes: Add selective prebuild cache keyed by package subgraph and toolchain stamp to reduce CI cold-start time.
Introduce lightweight node_modules virtualization to reuse cached artifacts without full installs.
New observability metrics: ci.prebuild_cache.hit_ratio and ci.prebuild_cache.restore_latency.
Nightly prune job to cap stored prebuild artifacts per repo and retention policy.
